newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 12.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- Prosecutors questioned Lee Sung-ho, a key associate of Kim Hyun-chul, the second son of President Kim Young-sam, on suspicions that he managed funds for the junior Kim.
- South Korea, host of the East Asian Games, won its first gold medal in swimming as Cho Kwang-jae beat Japan's Yoshiaki Okita in the 100m breaststroke finals. Cho Kwang-jae's record was 1:03.44.
- North Korea officially informed the Asian Development Bank of its intention to join the organisation last month, said Lee Bong-suh, a vice governor of the ADB.
- According to a senior official, the ruling party is pushing to pass a law that will honor those who were arrested or killed during a 1980 massacre in the southwest city of Kwangju.
